asks.raw_wording: vessel carrying weapons is anchored in beyond 24nm. Which convention, who takes action
asks.examiner_evidence: INDIVIDUALLY_ATTRIBUTED to Senthil (marker: Internal Senthil sir)
asks.question_identity: Which instrument governs a ship carrying weapons at anchor SEAWARD OF THE CONTIGUOUS ZONE, and which State may act. The 24 nm in the candidate's wording is the outer limit of the contiguous zone (UNCLOS Art 33), so the question is really about where coastal-State enforcement jurisdiction ENDS and flag-State jurisdiction stands alone.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: weapon/firearm/arms/PCASP over q-text returns 2 cards, both SUA-titled (QB1_A#q17, QB9_A#q7); neither addresses weapons carriage, jurisdiction by zone, or who may board. The UNCLOS zone cards QB1_A#q19-q23 give the zones but not this scenario.
asks.authority: UNCLOS Arts 3, 33, 56, 92, 110; SUA Convention 1988 and its 2005 Protocol, Arts 3bis and 8bis; IMO PCASP guidance MSC.1/Circ.1405/Rev.2 and MSC.1/Circ.1443.
asks.identity_notes: Legally sensitive and deliberately NOT reducible to 'beyond 24 nm weapons are legal'. The card must separate lawful PCASP carriage under flag-State law from a SUA 3bis offence, and must state that a third State may board seaward of the territorial sea only with flag-State authorisation under Art 8bis - the UNCLOS Art 110 right of visit does not list weapons carriage among its grounds. Anchor note: QB1_A carries 33 q-card divs but only 31 CANONICAL questions, so the next free canonical anchor is q32. Counting divs would have placed this card at q34 and left a gap.

asks.raw_wording: OWS not working just two days before arrival port, what is your 1st action- only single answer
asks.examiner_evidence: INDIVIDUALLY_ATTRIBUTED to Senthil (marker: Internal Senthil sir)
asks.question_identity: The examiner asked for ONE first action, not a procedure. The question tests whether the candidate stops the discharge before reaching for paperwork.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: OWS / oily water separator returns 0 q-text hits; 19 cards mention the OWS inside other answers (ORB, PSC, MARPOL documents) and none owns a defective-OWS scenario. 'bilge holding tank' returns 0.
asks.authority: MARPOL Annex I Regs 14, 15, 16 and 17; the Oil Record Book Part I regime; ISM Code 10.3 critical equipment and 9.1 non-conformity reporting.
asks.identity_notes: Single-answer discipline: stop the overboard discharge and retain the bilge water on board. Everything else - defect report, class and flag, repair, spares to the arrival port - follows, and must be offered as the chain AFTER the single answer, never instead of it. The card must never suggest an improvised discharge or a bypass.

asks.raw_wording: Type of vessel sailed - difference between chemical and oil product tanker to traditional oil tanker?
asks.question_identity: An engineering and operational comparison of a chemical or clean-product carrier against a crude oil carrier, asked off the back of 'type of vessel sailed' - so it is a ship-knowledge question, not a law question.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: product tanker / crude oil tanker / crude carrier returns 0 q-text hits. QB8_H#q2 (Type 1 vs Type 2 chemical tankers) and QB1_G#q33 (chemical tanker construction by type) both partition WITHIN chemical tankers; neither contrasts against a crude carrier.
asks.authority: MARPOL Annexes I and II; IBC Code; SOLAS II-2; the Certificate of Fitness regime.
asks.identity_notes: Bounded to the dimensions that actually differ and that a Chief Engineer owns: coatings and tank material, segregation and pumping, heating and cleanliness, venting and inerting, cargo diversity and previous-cargo history, and the certificate regime. Not an encyclopaedic tanker essay.

asks.raw_wording: primary and secondary means of venting
asks.question_identity: The named regulatory PAIR in SOLAS II-2/4.5.3.2 - the primary venting arrangement, and the independent secondary means that must prevent over- or under-pressure if the primary fails. This is the regulatory architecture, not the hardware inventory.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: QB8_A#q7 already owns tank venting hardware (P/V valve, mast riser, P/V breaker) under SOLAS II-2/4.5.3 and is the only card carrying the phrase 'secondary means' in a venting sense. A second venting card would duplicate the whole of it.
asks.authority: SOLAS II-2/4.5.3.2.1 and 4.5.3.2.2, and the parallel 11.6; IACS UI SC140.
asks.identity_notes: The examiner used the regulation's own vocabulary. The enrichment adds the two-tier framing and the two PERMITTED secondary options - a full-flow P/V valve, or a per-tank pressure sensor with alarm, the sensor being acceptable only where a full-flow P/V valve is the primary means - which is the limb the existing card does not carry.

asks.raw_wording: ETS - emergency towing system - time requirement for deployment
asks.question_identity: The deployment-time figures for emergency towing arrangements on tankers. The limb IS specific and IS examinable - it did not need to be held.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: 'emergency towing' returns 0 q-text hits; 4 body mentions, all inside amendment-overview or salvage cards (QB10_B#q1, QB10_B#q5, QB1_B#q11, QB9_A#q6). No card carries the arrangement, the times or the strengths.
asks.authority: SOLAS II-1/3-4 - arrangements for tankers of 20,000 dwt and above, procedures for all ships of 500 GT and above under MSC.256(84), in force 1 Jan 2010 and 1 Jan 2012 for existing cargo ships; IMO Res. MSC.35(63) paras 2.3.1, 2.4, 2.8.2, 3.1.1 and 3.1.3; MSC.1/Circ.1255/Rev.1 approved at MSC 110 (2025).
asks.identity_notes: VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY TEXT rather than inferred. MSC.35(63) 3.1.1 - the aft arrangement should be pre-rigged and capable of being deployed in a controlled manner in harbour conditions in not more than 15 min; 3.1.3 - the forward arrangement in not more than 1 h. Also 2.3.1 - working strength at least 1,000 kN for 20,000 to under 50,000 dwt and at least 2,000 kN for 50,000 dwt and over, working strength being one half ultimate strength.

asks.raw_wording: EUSRR - why it's required when there is hkc
asks.question_identity: Why a regional instrument survives the entry into force of the global one - a comparison question about scope, stringency and enforcement, not a description of either instrument.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: the bank knows both instruments - HKC in QB3_C#q3, QB3_F#q5 and QB3_H#q4; the EU SRR named in QB1_A#q16, QB3_C#q3, QB3_D#q1, QB3_G#q3 and QB3_H#q5 - but no card puts them side by side or answers 'why both'.
asks.authority: Regulation (EU) No 1257/2013; the Hong Kong Convention 2009, in force 26 June 2025; the European List of ship recycling facilities; the Basel Convention interface.
asks.identity_notes: Currency-sensitive and must be written as at August 2026, that is AFTER HKC entry into force. The comparison points: the EU SRR binds EU-flag ships wherever they recycle and reaches non-EU flags through the IHM and port-State limb; the European List is a positive list that a HKC Statement of Compliance does not automatically buy; the EU hazardous-materials list is wider; and the List requirement operates as a practical bar on beaching, which the HKC does not itself prohibit.

asks.raw_wording: Roro vessel latest amendments and cross questions.
asks.question_identity: The latest ro-ro-specific amendment package. This is NOT too broad to answer: as at August 2026 there is one clearly latest ro-ro package - the SOLAS II-2/20 and FSS Code fire-safety amendments for vehicle, special category and ro-ro spaces.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: ro-ro returns 0 q-text hits. The content EXISTS but is scattered - QB10_B#q1 carries the package correctly under MSC.550(108) and MSC.555(108), and QB2_F#q3 carries a one-line ro-ro limb. Neither is reachable by a candidate searching for ro-ro.
asks.authority: Res. MSC.550(108) amending SOLAS II-2/20 and Res. MSC.555(108) amending the FSS Code, in force 1 January 2026, applying to cargo ships and ro-ro passenger ships constructed on or after that date, with retroactive requirements on existing passenger ships by the first survey on or after 1 January 2028; the EMSA FIRESAFE studies as the driver.
asks.identity_notes: DEFECT FOUND WHILE SEARCHING, recorded separately rather than folded in: QB2_F#q3 attributes the ro-ro detection and cargo-control-room alarm requirements to MSC.532(107). MSC.532(107) is the PFOS, lifting appliance, inclinometer and Polar package. The ro-ro fire package is MSC.550(108), with the FSS amendments in MSC.555(108). QB10_B#q1 has it right, so the bank currently contradicts itself. This is the wrong-regulation-number trap class and is raised as OPEN-G1-010.

asks.raw_wording: ALARP. Why reduce ? why cant eliminate ?
asks.question_identity: ALARP as a named principle, with the examiner's own second limb - why risk is reduced rather than eliminated. The second limb is where the mark is.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: ALARP appears in 9 cards and 'grossly disproportionate' in 2 (QB4_J#q3, QB5_A#q10), but NO card's question is ALARP. A candidate searching the term lands inside a Risk Based Planning card. The 'why can it not be eliminated' limb is answered nowhere.
asks.authority: ISM Code 1.2.2.2; the hierarchy of control; the IMO FSA guidelines MSC-MEPC.2/Circ.12/Rev.2; UK HSE ALARP doctrine, cited as industry practice rather than as a maritime instrument.
asks.identity_notes: Written lean and explicitly cross-referenced to the existing risk-assessment cards so it adds the principle without re-teaching the matrix. Must not invent a convention that 'defines ALARP' - no IMO instrument does. ISM 1.2.2.2 is the duty; ALARP is the standard applied to discharging it.

asks.question_identity: Fire science. The four elements, and extinguishment by removing or disrupting one of them.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: 'tetrahedron' returns 0 across all 727 cards, in q-text and body alike. 'fire triangle' returns 0. This is a clean gap.
asks.authority: Fire science; SOLAS II-2 and the FSS Code for the shipboard media mapping. No regulatory citation is forced onto the definition itself.
asks.identity_notes: The mark is the fourth element - the chemical chain reaction - and mapping each extinguishing medium onto the side it attacks: cooling by water, smothering by CO2 and foam, starvation by isolation, and chain-breaking by dry powder and clean agents.

asks.question_identity: The instrument SET for a gas carrier, organised around what makes an LPG carrier different from any other ship - not a recitation of every maritime convention.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: 7 q-text hits across LPG, IGC and gas carrier - QB8_D#q1, QB2_I#q7, QB8_G#q2, QB8_H#q6, QB2_B#q6, QB8_F#q1 and QB6#q10. Each answers ONE instrument or system; none assembles the set or says which liability regime attaches.
asks.authority: SOLAS Chs II-2 and VII Part C; the IGC Code, mandatory through SOLAS VII/11; MARPOL Annexes I, II and VI; Load Lines; COLREG; STCW including Reg V/1-2 gas tanker training; ISM; ISPS; MLC; and the HNS Convention as the liability instrument.

asks.raw_wording: If you are assigning a job to 2E or 3E what all convention will apply
asks.question_identity: Which instruments are engaged when the Chief Engineer delegates a task to a junior engineer - competence, hours of rest, safe working, and where accountability sits.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: 'deleg' in q-text returns 2 cards, both about FLAG-STATE delegation to a Recognised Organisation (QB1_B#q7, QB3_B#q9) - a different sense of the word entirely. QB4_A#q22 is 2/E-to-CE progression. No card answers shipboard delegation.
asks.authority: STCW Reg I/14 and the Chapter III competence tables A-III/1 and A-III/2, and Section A-VIII/1 hours of rest; ISM Code 6.1 to 6.7 and 7; MLC 2006 Reg 2.3 and Title 4; SOLAS Ch. IX; and the company SMS standing orders and permit-to-work system.
asks.identity_notes: Must NOT invent an instrument that says 'the Chief Engineer may delegate X to a 2/E'. None does. The correct architecture is: STCW sets what the person is certificated and competent to do; ISM 6 requires the company to ensure personnel are qualified and familiarised; ISM 7 requires the procedure for the task; MLC bounds the hours; and the delegating officer retains accountability for the decision to delegate.

asks.question_identity: The subdivision datum. The trap is temporal: the margin line is the operative limit in the DETERMINISTIC framework, and ships to which the 2009 harmonised SOLAS II-1 applies are assessed probabilistically instead.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: 'margin line' appears exactly once in the whole corpus, in passing inside QB1_supplementary#q3 (A >= R). No card defines it. QB1_supplementary#q9 (factor of subdivision) is the nearest neighbour and is itself deterministic-era.
asks.authority: SOLAS II-1 - the classical definition, a line at least 76 mm below the upper surface of the bulkhead deck at side, and the deterministic floodable-length and factor-of-subdivision framework; SOLAS II-1 Part B-1 as amended by MSC.216(82), in force 1 January 2009, for the probabilistic method.
asks.identity_notes: Must not teach the deterministic formulation as universally current, and must not claim the term is abolished either. The honest frame is: what it is, the regime in which it governs, which ships still sit in that regime, and what replaced it for ships built on or after 1 January 2009.

asks.raw_wording: can you pump out sw (or Fw) directly from cargo hold.
asks.question_identity: A bulk-carrier hold question. 'Directly' is the operative word: the examiner is testing whether the candidate knows hold bilges are pumped through a controlled route, and only after the water's character is established.
asks.live_corpus_search: Live-727: hold bilge / cargo hold bilge returns 0 q-text hits. QB2_A carries the bulk-cargo cluster - q10 IMSBC, q13 cohesive cargo, q27 liquefaction, q28 ore, coal and grain - but nothing on hold water.
asks.authority: MARPOL Annex I Regs 15 and 34 and the definition of oily bilge water; MARPOL Annex V Regs 4 and 6 and the cargo-residue and hold-washing regime including HME cargoes; the ship's approved Garbage Management Plan; SOLAS II-1/35-1 bilge pumping arrangements.
asks.identity_notes: Resolved from evidence rather than assumed: the candidate wrote 'sw (or Fw) ... directly from cargo hold', so the context is water that has entered a hold, not tank ballast. The answer turns on contamination status, and on the fact that hold bilges are led to the bilge system rather than to a direct overboard line.
